prompt: Company profile: Convenience store operator in Las Cruces, New Mexico; 15 employees across two stores. Situation: The company is replacing two aging 10,000-gallon gasoline underground storage tanks at one store with new double-walled tanks, and permanently closing the old ones. New Mexico administers a state UST program. Ask: Identify the compliance obligations this situation creates or affects for the compliance-obligations register. For each obligation: state the requirement, its source, its applicability to this company, the ISO clause it maps to (ISO 14001 6.1.3 / ISO 45001 6.1.3), and how and when compliance should be evaluated (9.1.2).
response:
**Compliance Obligations Register: UST Replacement Project**
*Company: Convenience Store Operator, Las Cruces, NM | Activity: Permanent closure of two 10,000-gal gasoline USTs and installation of new double-walled tanks*

---

| # | Requirement | Source (Regulation/Standard) | Applicability to Company | ISO Clause Mapping | Compliance Evaluation Method & Frequency (9.1.2) |
|---|-------------|------------------------------|--------------------------|-------------------|---------------------------------------------------|
| **1** | **Pre-Closure Notification & Permit**: Submit written notice to NMED at least 30 days prior to permanent closure; obtain closure permit before commencing work. | 20.5.2.9 NMAC (Notification); 20.5.4 NMAC (Closure) | Mandatory for permanent closure of two existing 10,000-gallon gasoline USTs. | ISO 14001 6.1.3 | **Method**: Document review of submitted notification letter and NMED-issued permit. **Frequency**: Verify completion before any closure activities begin; re-verify during project kickoff meeting. |
| **2** | **Closure Site Assessment**: Conduct site assessment for soil/groundwater contamination; collect samples from excavation bottom and sidewalls; submit results to NMED for approval. | 20.5.4.12–.13 NMAC (Closure Site Assessment) | Mandatory for all UST permanent closures to determine if corrective action is required. | ISO 14001 6.1.3 | **Method**: Review laboratory analytical reports and NMED's written approval of assessment. **Frequency**: Within 30 days of assessment completion; verify before backfilling excavation. |
| **3** | **Installation Permit & Notification**: Obtain UST installation permit from NMED; notify NMED at least 30 days prior to installation. | 20.5.2.9 NMAC (Notification); 20.5.3 NMAC (Installation) | Mandatory for installation of two new 10,000-gallon double-walled tanks. | ISO 14001 6.1.3 | **Method**: Document review of permit application and NMED approval. **Frequency**: Verify permit issuance before contractor mobilization; confirm 30-day notice sent. |
| **4** | **Certified Contractor Requirement**: Use NMED-certified contractors for all closure and installation activities; maintain proof of certification. | 20.5.3.8 NMAC (Installation); 20.5.4.9 NMAC (Closure) | Directly applicable to both closure and installation work. | ISO 14001 6.1.3 & ISO 45001 6.1.3 | **Method**: Review contractor certification cards and NMED registry verification. **Frequency**: Before contract signing and contractor site entry; maintain records for duration of project. |
| **5** | **Financial Assurance**: Maintain valid financial assurance mechanism (insurance, guarantee, or trust fund) for corrective action and third-party liability throughout project and operation. | 20.5.6 NMAC (Financial Responsibility) | Required for all UST owners/operators; must cover both old tank closure and new tank operation. | ISO 14001 6.1.3 | **Method**: Review current financial assurance instrument and annual certification. **Frequency**: Annually at minimum; verify coverage extends to project period and new tanks before installation. |
| **6** | **OSHA Excavation Safety (Trenching & Shoring)**: Implement protective systems for excavations >5 ft; designate competent person; obtain excavation permit if required; perform daily inspections. | 29 CFR 1926.650–652 (OSHA Excavation Standards) | Mandatory for all excavation work associated with tank removal and installation. | ISO 45001 6.1.3 | **Method**: Site inspection by competent person; review excavation permit and daily inspection logs. **Frequency**: Daily before and during each shift; audit during monthly safety inspection. |
| **7** | **OSHA Confined Space Entry**: Implement permit-required confined space program if workers enter tanks or excavations >4 ft deep with limited egress; atmospheric testing required. | 29 CFR 1910.146 (OSHA Confined Space) | Applicable if workers enter old tanks during closure or new tanks during installation. | ISO 45001 6.1.3 | **Method**: Review entry permits, atmospheric monitoring data, and rescue plan. **Frequency**: For each entry; audit program quarterly. |
| **8** | **Spill Prevention & Immediate Release Reporting**: Prevent spills during transfer of product and excavation; report any release >25 gallons or any size that reaches soil/water immediately to NMED and local authorities. | 20.5.5 NMAC (Release Response); 20.5.5.9 NMAC (Spill Prevention Plan) | Applicable during pumping old tanks and installing new tanks. | ISO 14001 6.1.3 | **Method**: Review spill prevention plan; verify spill kit availability; check incident logs. **Frequency**: Before project start; daily during active fuel handling; audit annually. |
| **9** | **New UST Installation Standards**: Install tanks per NMED specifications (double-walled, cathodic protection, spill/overfill prevention equipment, sump testing). | 20.5.3 NMAC; 20.5.101 NMAC (New Tank Standards) | Directly applicable to new double-walled tank installation. | ISO 14001 6.1.3 | **Method**: Inspect installation; review contractor completion certificates and NMED inspection sign-off. **Frequency**: During installation (hold points); final inspection before placing in service. |
| **10** | **Tank Tightness & Integrity Testing**: New tanks must pass pre-installation and post-installation tightness testing; double-wall interstitial monitoring must be operational. | 20.5.3.10 NMAC (Testing) | Mandatory before placing new tanks into service. | ISO 14001 6.1.3 | **Method**: Review certified test results and NMED acceptance. **Frequency**: After installation, before fuel delivery; verify annually thereafter. |
| **11** | **UST Registration**: Register new USTs with NMED within 30 days of installation; update tank ownership records. | 20.5.2.11 NMAC (Registration) | Required for new tanks at existing facility. | ISO 14001 6.1.3 | **Method**: Document review of NMED registration certificate. **Frequency**: Within 30 days of installation; verify during next annual compliance review. |
| **12** | **Hazard Communication & PPE**: Provide Safety Data Sheets (SDS) for gasoline; train workers on hazards; ensure proper PPE (respirators, protective clothing) during tank work. | 29 CFR 1910.1200 (HazCom); 29 CFR 1910.132–138 (PPE) | All workers handling gasoline or entering excavation/tank areas. | ISO 45001 6.1.3 | **Method**: Review SDS availability, training records, and PPE assessments. **Frequency**: Before project start; verify during weekly safety inspections. |
| **13** | **Local Fire Code Permit**: Obtain permit from Las Cruces Fire Department (or Doña Ana County Fire) for hot work, tank installation, and hazardous materials handling. | IFC Chapter 57 / Las Cruces Municipal Code (Local Authority) | Required for installation project within city limits. | ISO 14001 6.1.3 & ISO 45001 6.1.3 | **Method**: Review fire department permit and inspection sign-offs. **Frequency**: Before hot work or tank installation; verify during project closeout. |
| **14** | **Record Retention**: Maintain closure reports, assessment data, installation certificates, and permits for minimum 3 years (closure) and life of tank (installation). | 20.5.7 NMAC (Recordkeeping) | Applies to all UST project documentation. | ISO 14001 6.1.3 | **Method**: Audit records management system; verify retention schedule compliance. **Frequency**: Annually during records audit; at project completion. |
| **15** | **Release Detection Operation**: Install and maintain continuous leak detection (interstitial monitoring) on new double-walled tanks; test alarm functionality monthly. | 20.5.4 NMAC (Release Detection) | Mandatory for all new UST systems. | ISO 14001 6.1.3 | **Method**: Review monthly monitoring records and alarm test logs. **Frequency**: Monthly operational checks; annual third-party compliance audit. |

---

**Notes for 9.1.2 Implementation:**
- **Pre-project**: Verify all permits, certifications, and plans before work begins.
- **During project**: Conduct daily safety inspections (OSHA) and environmental oversight; maintain photo documentation.
- **Post-project**: Obtain all final approvals and test results within 30 days; update compliance register.
- **Ongoing**: Annual compliance audit of financial assurance, release detection, and record retention; integrate findings into management review (ISO 14001/45001 9.3).
